claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
Pulumi derives resource ordering from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready and independent resources deploy in parallel.

Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind (per pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go); chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.

The Helm docs state that "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's kind_sorter hardcoded list begins with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-sorted list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies don't change ordering: a subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind.
Helm chart hooks are ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations, and hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release.
HIP-0025 proposes native sequencing for resources and subcharts in Helm and is still a draft.

In Pulumi, passing an output or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in the dependency graph; the Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to be ready before creating dependents, deploys independent resources in parallel, and deletes follow the graph in reverse.
Pulumi's helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for outside dependencies.
Pulumi's parallel deployment makes updates faster than a strict serial sequence.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi with Helm.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after its dependencies.
There are three common ways to adopt Pulumi alongside or in place of Helm; using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.

helm.v4.Chart registers each rendered Kubernetes object as a Pulumi resource so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state; helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release preserving hooks, post-rendering, and release history.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts by kind, and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart dependency doesn't make it install first.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated; Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision and helm rollback restores a prior revision.
Pulumi Policies is open source with rules in Python, TypeScript, or OPA Rego; the Enterprise edition adds Pulumi-maintained policy packs for CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and NIST.
